passage:
I was visiting my neighbour when her son Vaibhav, five, knocked over his milk. A thin crack ran down the side of his glass. When his mother came back from the balcony, Vaibhav stood in front of the puddle. "I didn't spill. It was already like this."
She pointed at the glass. "And this?"
"It was never cracked," he said, very fast, hands behind his back.
I can't know what he was thinking. But his lip was shaking, and when she said, "I'm not angry, I just need to know," he whispered, "It slipped."
— Yamini

qa.q: Where did Vaibhav stand when his mother came back?
qa.a: In front of the puddle.

qa.q: What was Vaibhav afraid of when he said the glass was never cracked?
qa.a: He seemed afraid of getting into trouble, and saying it hadn't happened may have felt like a way to make the spill disappear.

qa.q: Which words of his mother's changed the moment?
qa.a: "I'm not angry, I just need to know" lowered the fear enough for Vaibhav to whisper the truth.

qa.q: How might Vaibhav's mother feel hearing 'it was never cracked' with the crack right in front of her?
qa.a: She may feel puzzled or a bit frustrated at first, but her calm reply suggests she understood he was scared.

grounding: A neighbour sees a five-year-old deny a spill and a cracked glass out of fear, until his mother makes it safe to tell.

passage:
Tuesday. Aadhya, five, knocked Nani's blue cup off the table, and a chip broke off the rim. When Nani asked, Aadhya shook her head hard. "It was always like that." Her big brother Yash said nothing. That night she took a long time to fall asleep.
Thursday. Aadhya spilled juice on the sofa and said, "Not me," before anyone had asked. Nani lifted her onto her lap. "Spills happen. We just wipe them up together."
Next Sunday. A plate slipped from her hands. Aadhya froze, then called, "Nani! I dropped it. Can you help?"

qa.q: What broke off Nani's blue cup?
qa.a: A chip broke off the rim.

qa.q: Why did Aadhya say 'Not me' before anyone asked?
qa.a: Aadhya was scared of being in trouble again, so denying it first felt like a way to stay safe.

qa.q: What turning point helped Aadhya own up on Sunday?
qa.a: Nani's calm "We just wipe them up together" on Thursday showed Aadhya that admitting a spill wouldn't bring trouble.

qa.q: How might Nani feel on Sunday when Aadhya calls for help?
qa.a: Nani is probably relieved and pleased that Aadhya trusted her enough to say she dropped the plate 😊

grounding: Over a week a five-year-old who denied chipping a cup out of fear learns from her grandmother's calm that owning up is safe.

passage:
Guests were due in ten minutes, and the fan had just stopped in a power cut. Chandrika was lighting candles when she saw a dark stain spreading across the new tablecloth. Her son Sachin, six, stood next to it holding an empty cup.
"Did you spill the juice?"
"No."
"Sachin, the cup's empty and your hand is sticky."
"It didn't spill. The cloth was already like that." His eyes flicked to the door.
Chandrika took a breath. There was no time for a lecture anyway. She knelt. "Spills are okay. Help me flip the cloth over?"
Sachin grabbed a corner at once, and as they tugged, he mumbled, "I bumped it."

qa.q: What was Sachin holding when Chandrika saw the stain?
qa.a: An empty cup.

qa.q: Why does Sachin insist the cloth was already like that?
qa.a: With guests coming and everything rushed, Sachin seems scared of being in trouble, so denying the spill feels as if it might undo it 😰

qa.q: What choice under time pressure helped Sachin own up?
qa.a: Chandrika skipped the lecture, said spills were okay and gave Sachin a job flipping the cloth, which made admitting it feel safe.

qa.q: What are those ten minutes like for Chandrika?
qa.a: Chandrika is juggling a power cut, candles and arriving guests, and still has to choose calm over scolding.

grounding: With guests arriving in a power cut, a six-year-old denies spilling juice out of fear until his mother makes it safe to admit.

passage: At Vinita aunty's flat next door in Lucknow, Rafiq, five, was carrying her blue cup to the sink when it bumped the tap. A thin crack ran down its side, and milk dripped on the floor. Vinita aunty came in. Rafiq put the cup behind his back. "It's not cracked." "Can I see?" "It was always like that." He stood on the milk puddle with his sock. "I didn't spill." His eyes stayed fixed on her face. Vinita aunty knelt down. "Rafiq, cups crack. I'm not angry. Let's wipe it together." His shoulders dropped. "It bumped," he whispered.

qa.q: What did the cup bump into?
qa.a: The tap.

qa.q: Why did Rafiq say the cup was always like that?
qa.a: He was afraid of getting into trouble, so pretending the crack wasn't there felt safer than saying what happened.

qa.q: Which words from Vinita aunty helped Rafiq tell the truth, and why?
qa.a: "Cups crack. I'm not angry. Let's wipe it together" took away his fear of trouble, so he could admit it bumped.

qa.q: How might Vinita aunty feel seeing Rafiq stand on the milk with his sock?
qa.a: She might feel a mix of amusement and tenderness, understanding he was scared rather than trying to trick her.

grounding: A young child insists a cracked cup was never cracked and denies spilling, because fear of trouble outweighs accuracy.

passage: "Ojas, why is there juice on the sofa?" "There's no juice, Papa." "This orange patch here?" "It was already there." "Your glass is empty." "I drank it." "All of it went in your mouth?" "Yes. I didn't spill anything." "Ojas, look at me. Are you worried I'll be angry?" Ojas stared at his socks. "...Yes." "I won't be. Spills happen. I spilled tea on this same sofa last month." "You did?" "Ask Amma. Now, shall we get the cloth together?" "It was a small spill." "I know. Small spills are easy to clean." Harish handed him the cloth. Ojas scrubbed very hard.

qa.q: Where was the orange patch?
qa.a: On the sofa.

qa.q: What was Ojas worried about when he said "I didn't spill anything"?
qa.a: He was worried Papa would be angry, and that fear felt bigger than telling what happened.

qa.q: What was the turning point that helped Ojas admit the spill?
qa.a: Papa asking if he was worried and saying he wouldn't be angry, even sharing his own tea spill, so Ojas felt safe.

qa.q: How might Harish feel watching Ojas scrub very hard?
qa.a: Harish might feel tender and a bit amused, seeing that Ojas wants to make things right once the fear is gone.

grounding: A young child denies a spill in front of the evidence because fear of trouble outweighs wanting to be accurate.
